title: markdown-serve project config
description: Per-project settings in .markdown-serve.json, at the directory passed to markdown-serve. A missing file, or a missing key, uses the default shown on each property. Unknown keys are ignored when the file is loaded.

$schema.description: Location of this schema, so editors can validate and explain the file. markdown-serve init writes the URL of markdown-serve.schema.json.

ignore.description: Root-relative paths left out of the code-documentation cache and out of the scan that decides which languages are present. `*` matches one path segment, `**` matches across segments (`**/` also matches zero segments). Prefix an entry with `re:` to use a regular expression, which is searched rather than anchored. The cache directory is always ignored. The language scan also skips dot-directories and .git, .venv, node_modules, __pycache__, .tox, .mypy_cache, and .cache.

codedoc.description: Code-documentation cache. The viewer runs without it; build it with `markdown-serve build-cache`.

cache_dir.description: Project-relative directory where generated markdown is written. Leading and trailing slashes are stripped. Pages are still opened at the source path, not under this directory. Add the directory to .gitignore.

languages.description: Languages to document. `cpp` uses libclang and compile_commands.json. `python` uses the stdlib ast module and needs nothing else. A non-empty list is explicit: each entry is kept even when the tree has no source files for it, and a missing tool is reported. Omit this key to use cpp and python and drop a language that has no source files.

jobs.description: How many processes parse source files in parallel. null uses one process per CPU. Any other value is ignored and a warning is printed.

cpp.description: C++ backend. Read only when cpp is an active language.

compile_commands.description: Project-relative path to the compilation database. Each listed source file is parsed with that entry's compiler flags.

libclang.description: Shared library used to parse C++. A string is a path to libclang.so, libclang.dylib, or libclang.dll, or to a directory that contains one of those. null, or a blank string, searches $LIBCLANG_PATH, then `llvm-config --libdir`, then /usr/local/lib and /usr/lib/llvm-*/lib, then the libclang wheel installed by `uv sync --extra cpp`.
